**Reasoning:**

- **C2 (clear winner).** It has the strongest sustained speed gradient: a Gaussian "tracking toward 9 m/s" term (weight 2.0, σ=3.5) that still yields ~0.4–0.5 reward per m/s at current speeds, plus an unclipped linear term (0.2·v_x), on top of the tanh term. It also has a linear (not just tanh) push beyond the current plateau, plus hinge-style tilt/lateral penalties and a fall penalty that keep the gait stable instead of collapsing. Its task_score is already 7.54 at iter 500 and still climbing steadily (~+0.3/50 iters), well ahead of the pack.

- **C4 (second).** Purely speed-focused with a linear term that keeps pressure all the way to 15 m/s (unlike C1's surge ramp, which saturates at 9.5 m/s). Weak but active tilt cost and negligible regularizers mean little drag on top speed. It already leads the non-C2 candidates (6.54) and, because its speed gradient stays flat/positive at high speed, it should keep improving.

- **C1 (third).** Good posture shaping (upright exp term, heading alignment, alive bonus) that prevents falls, but its speed shaping is the most saturating of the three (tanh temp 6 plus a surge ramp that caps at 9.5 m/s), so beyond ~9 m/s it loses essentially all speed pressure. It was the slowest riser early and its task_score is still climbing only weakly (6.00).

- **C4/C1 vs C3.** C3's speed terms are extremely weakly scaled (tanh temp 10 → ~0.1/m/s gradient, high-speed bonus only 0.3 over a 9 m/s span ≈ 0.033/m/s), so its reward carries almost no incremental pressure beyond ~6 m/s; its task_score has already flat-lined (6.16 → 6.16) and the always-active soft joint-limit penalty further constrains gait extension. It should end last.
